title: Environmental issues caused by information systems
competency: Explain the environmental harm of devices and e-waste, and how e-waste management, green technology and paperless systems reduce it.

keywords.def: Discarded electronic devices; they contain toxic materials such as cadmium, lead and mercury.
A systematic procedure for gathering e-waste, recovering and recycling material safely, and disposing of it with minimal harm.
Environmentally friendly (clean) technology that monitors or reduces the negative impact of technology on the environment.
Using email, online portals and applications instead of paper records.

en.text: Technologies use a lot of resources and power, and electronic devices contain non-biodegradable materials and toxic heavy metals such as cadmium, lead and mercury. These can leak into the ground and contaminate our water, plants and animals. E-waste management is a systematic procedure for gathering e-waste, recovering and recycling materials safely, and disposing of the rest with minimal harm to the environment.

screens.title: A buried battery
screens.ask: An old phone and its battery are thrown into a farm field. Over the years, what is the main danger?
opts: Toxic metals leak into soil and water

Dispose of the rest in a way that minimises harm to the environment.

en.text: The harm technology does to the environment led to green or clean technologies that monitor or reduce that harm, moving towards a sustainable, low-carbon economy. Examples are solar panels, electric vehicles, smart meters and wind turbines. Paperless systems such as email and online portals reduce cutting trees for paper, and online collaboration lets experts work together without travelling, cutting carbon emissions.

screens.title: Green (clean) technology
paras: Environmental harm led to new environmentally friendly technologies.
Aim: a sustainable, low-carbon economy.
Green technology monitors or reduces the negative impact of technology on the environment.
Book examples: solar panels, electric vehicles, smart meters, wind turbines.
The book also lists natural gas, but it is a fossil fuel, not a clean technology.

screens.title: Paperless systems and virtual laboratories
paras: Email, online portals and apps reduce the cutting of trees for paper.
Figure 1.13: paper-based systems increase deforestation; paperless systems reduce it.
Information systems make a worldwide virtual laboratory.
Experts share research and ideas without meeting in person.
This cuts the carbon emissions of travelling.

screens.text: Which action makes a student an "environment ambassador"?

screens.text: A school office prints 500 pages of forms every week and stores them in cabinets. Which change helps the environment most?

notes.text: p.11 lists "natural gas" as a green technology. Natural gas is a fossil fuel that releases CO₂ when burned; at most it is a lower-carbon transition fuel. The lesson teaches it as not green.
